newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief welcomes US approval of chemical accord.
newsitem.headline: UN chief welcomes US approval of chemical accord.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Friday welcomed approval by the United States Senate of the chemical weapons treaty, saying he looked forward to receiving the formal ratification papers.

"The potential of this significant agreement to strengthen international peace and security depends on the degree of universality it achieves," he said in a statement. "I look forward, therefore, to formal ratification of the convention by the United States, as well as by other states which have not yet done so."

The formal papers, known as "instruments of ratification," must be deposited at United Nations headquarters in New York. U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said 164 countries had signed the treaty and 76, excluding the United States, will have deposited the papers by the end of Friday.

The U.S. Senate voted 74-26 on Thursday in favour of ratifying the Chemical Weapons Convention, which prohibits the development, production and use of chemical arms. The treaty comes into force on April 29 and the first conference of parties to the treaty will open on May 6 in the Hague.
The United States and Russia are the world's largest possessors of chemical weapons, with declared stocks of 70,000 tons between them. But Russia is among those that have not ratified the treaty.
